expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: "No — confirmation modals are **detection-level** controls (rung 2/5 on the poka-yoke ladder). They catch mistakes but don't prevent them"

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: "users habitually click through after a few deletions" and "Users develop 'click-through muscle memory'"

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: "**Soft delete** (substitution, rung 4) — 'deleted' workspaces move to a Trash folder, auto-purge after 30 days"; final rec: "Soft-delete as default"

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
expectations.evidence: "**Undo toast** ... Show 'Workspace deleted. **Undo**' for 10 seconds post-delete. One-click recovery."

expectations.text: Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: "**Hard-delete friction** (forcing function, rung 3) — Require typing the workspace name to permanently delete."

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: Mentions "confirmation + name entry" for permanent delete, but never requires the dialog to display the workspace name or the scale/quantity of data being destroyed

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: No mention of server-side/API enforcement; all controls described are UI-level (modal, toast, menu, trash folder)

expectations.text: Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: "**Recommendation:** Soft-delete as default + optional hard-delete behind friction" — singles out a top choice over the numbered alternatives
